chapter.title: Classes
chapter.para: This chapter describes the public classes of net.cls: NetGlobal, whose instance is the environment object &net;, NetObject, the class of every .NET object in Rexx, its subclasses NetType, NetArray and NetEnum, and the helper classes NetNamespace, NetRef, NetTyped, NetHandler, NetEvent and NetCall. The event thread's classes are described in .
Every method of these classes is UNGUARDED: a NetObject can be used from several Rexx threads at once, as its .NET object can be used from several .NET threads (if the .NET type allows it).

section.title: NetGlobal Class (the .net Object)
section.para: The single instance of NetGlobal, made when net.cls is loaded, is the environment object &net;: the root of .NET's namespaces (it is a NetNamespace), and the bridge's helpers, as methods. The helpers live on &net; rather than on .NET objects, so that no .NET member is hidden by them: every message to a .NET object goes to .NET.

example.title: .net — introspection
example.programlisting:
sb = .net~System~Text~StringBuilder~new("abc") say .net~typeOf(sb) .net~typeObject(sb)~Name say .net~isInstance(sb, "System.Object") .net~isInstance(sb, .net~System~String) say .net~members(.net~System~Math)~section(1, 4)~makeString("L", " ") say .net~load("System.Xml")~word(1) say .net~type("System.Environment+SpecialFolder")~Desktop
::requires "net.cls"
example.screen: System.Text.StringBuilder StringBuilder 1 0 Abs Acos Acosh Asin System.Xml, Desktop

section.title: Namespace or Type
section.para: Any message that is not one of the methods below is the name of a namespace or of a type at the root of .NET's namespaces: .net~System, .net~Microsoft, a namespace of a loaded assembly, or a type in no namespace. The answer is a NetNamespace or a NetType, remembered once found (). A name that is neither is an error. A namespace takes no arguments.

section.title: addHandler
section.para: Adds handler to the event named event (caseless) of the .NET object or type object: the same as object~Event += handler (). handler is a NetHandler, or a .NET delegate of the event's type. See also .

section.title: as
section.para: Returns value marked as the .NET type, a NetType or a type's name as takes it: a . Given to .NET, the value is converted to that type, and the overload that takes it is chosen (). It forces any type: an enum, a nullable type, an interface, or a delegate type for a NetHandler (.net~as(h, "System.Func<int>")).

section.title: box
section.para: Returns a new .NET object holding value converted to type, as a NetObject (). The argument order is BSF4ooRexx's box. type is a NetType, a name as type takes it ("short", "System.UInt32", an enum), or one of these indicators, caseless and shortened down to their capitals:

listitem.para: BOolean, BYte (.NET's Byte, unsigned), Char, Double, Float (Single), Int (Int32), Long (Int64), Object (the value as it would go to an object parameter), SHort (Int16), STring.
BO, BY, CHAR, DE (Decimal), DO, INT16, UINT16, INT32, UINT32, INT64, UINT64, SB (SByte), SI (Single), ST, and the long names (Boolean, Character, Decimal...).

section.para: A value that does not fit the type is an error. A reference type and &nil; give &nil;. See also .

section.title: createObject
section.para: Windows only. Returns a new COM object of the class progid ("Excel.Application", "Scripting.Dictionary"), reached through IDispatch, as ooRexx's OLEObject reaches it. language is the language of every call to it: English (US) by default, as VBA; "user", the user's, as OLEObject; or a culture name ("es-ES"). See .

section.title: eventLoop
section.para: Takes the calls of queued handlers, as they arrive, and dispatches each on this thread, until (). While it waits, the thread holds no interpreter lock, and on Windows COM delivers its events to it.

section.title: events
section.para: Returns an Array with the names of the events of object: a .NET object, a type (its static events), or a COM object (its source interfaces' events).

section.title: extend
section.para: Makes a .NET type that derives from base and implements the interfaces, whose virtual and abstract members are the Rexx class's methods; returns it, a NetType. class is a subclass of NetObject, extended once; base and the interfaces are NetTypes or names. If base is an interface, the new type derives from System.Object and implements it. See .

section.title: int16, int32, ... (Forced Types)
section.para: typename is one of int16, int32, int64, uint16, uint32, uint64, byte, sbyte, single, double, decimal, bool, char and string. Each returns value marked as a .NET type, a : int16 System.Int16, int32 System.Int32, int64 System.Int64, uint16, uint32 and uint64 their unsigned types, byte System.Byte, sbyte System.SByte, single System.Single, double System.Double, decimal System.Decimal, bool System.Boolean, char System.Char, and string System.String (without an argument, .net~string describes &net;). The value is converted when it goes to .NET, which chooses the overload that takes that type ().

section.title: get
section.para: Returns the property or field name of object (a .NET object, or a type for a static member), or the result of its method of that name with no arguments, taking the name exactly as written: no case is guessed, and a Rexx method of the same name does not get in the way. A name that is no member is SYNTAX 97.1. See also and .

section.title: getActiveObject
section.para: Windows only. Returns the running instance of the COM class progid (VBA's GetObject(, "Excel.Application"): an Excel opened by hand), an error if none is running. language as for . See .

section.title: getConstant
section.para: Windows only. Returns the constant name (caseless) of the type library that the COM object object comes from, as OLEObject's getConstant: .net~getConstant(excel, "xlHAlignRight"); &nil; if there is none. Without a name, all of them, a StringTable. See .

section.title: getKnownEvents
section.para: Windows only. Returns the events of the COM object object as OLEObject's getKnownEvents does, the same stem; &nil; if it has none. See .

section.title: getKnownMethods
section.para: Windows only. Returns the methods and properties of the COM object object as OLEObject's getKnownMethods does, the same stem, with also !PROGID and !CLSID (OLEObject's progid and clsid); &nil; if it has no type information. See .

section.title: getObject
section.para: Windows only. Returns the COM object that moniker names, as OLEObject's GetObject and VBA's GetObject(path) give it: a document file (opened by its application), WMI through "winmgmts:", any display name. language as for . See .

section.title: handleCount
section.para: Returns the number of .NET objects that Rexx holds now (live handles), for diagnostics: a number that keeps growing in a loop means proxies that are kept somewhere.

section.title: handler
section.para: Returns a : the Rexx object and the name of one of its methods, message, for .NET to call. Where .NET wants a delegate (an Action, a Func, a Comparison, an EventHandler, any delegate type), it becomes a delegate of that type, which sends the message to the object with the delegate's arguments. options is a string of blank-separated words, caseless:

listitem.para: The call is queued, and the delegate returns at once; a Rexx thread takes it with or .
Queued, keeping only the newest call of this handler that has not been taken yet.

section.para: Without options, the call runs at once, on the thread .NET calls from. See .

section.title: invoke
section.para: Calls the method name of object (a .NET object, or a type for a static method) with the arguments, taking the name exactly as written, and returns its result, if any. The name may carry type arguments in C# syntax, for a generic method ("Empty<int>"), or be an event's accessor ("add_Click"). A name that is no member is SYNTAX 97.1. It reaches members that a Rexx method hides ().

section.title: isInstance
section.para: Returns &true; if object is a .NET object of type (a NetType or a name), or of a type derived from it or implementing it; &false; otherwise, also for a Rexx value or &nil;, which are no .NET objects.

section.title: load
section.para: Loads an assembly, by name ("System.Xml"; one the runtime does not know is looked for as name.dll in the current directory, then next to the bridge) or by the path of its .dll, and returns its full name. Its types are then found by name. See .

section.title: members
section.para: Returns an Array with the names of the public members of object: instance members for an object, static ones for a type, each name once, sorted.

section.title: named
section.para: Windows only. Returns a named argument for a method of a COM object, VBA's name:=value: excel~Workbooks~Open(file, .net~named("ReadOnly", .true)). Named arguments go anywhere among the others. See .

section.title: namespace
section.para: Returns the namespace whose full name is name ("System.IO"), exactly, as a NetNamespace: the way to a namespace whose first part is also the name of a method of &net;.

section.title: new
section.para: Returns a new instance of type, a NetType, made by its constructor that takes the arguments: the same as type~new(arguments).

section.title: nextEvent
section.para: Returns the next queued call of a handler, a , waiting for one up to seconds (a number, fractions allowed), or, without it, as long as needed; &nil; if none came in time. While it waits, the thread holds no interpreter lock, and on Windows COM delivers its events to it. See .

section.title: null
section.para: Returns a null of no particular type, a NetTyped: &nil; does the same for most parameters, and .net~as(.nil, type) gives the null a type when overloads compete.

section.title: queuedCalls
section.para: Returns the number of queued calls that no Rexx thread has taken yet, for diagnostics.

section.title: ref
section.para: Returns a new holding value (default &nil;), for a ref, out or in parameter of a .NET method, or an argument by reference of a COM method ().

section.title: releaseObject
section.para: Windows only. Releases the COM object object now (Marshal.FinalReleaseComObject), so that its server (an Excel process) can end at once, rather than at .NET's next garbage collection. The proxy remains, and cannot be used any more.

section.title: removeHandler
section.para: Removes handler from the event event of object: the same as object~Event -= handler. The handler must be the same NetHandler object that was added.

section.title: set
section.para: Sets the property or field name of object (a .NET object, or a type for a static member) to value, taking the name exactly as written. A name that is no member is SYNTAX 97.1.

section.title: stopEventLoop
section.para: Ends every running now, on any thread, once the call it is dispatching has returned.

section.title: type
section.para: Returns a type, a NetType:

listitem.para: by its full name, with C#'s aliases (int, string, object, bool, double...), generic types in C# syntax ("System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary<string, int>"), array types ("int[]", "string[,]") and nested types ("System.Environment+SpecialFolder"). A type found by name is remembered, and the same object each time.
an open generic type (a name such as "System.Collections.Generic.List`1", or a NetType) and its type arguments, each a NetType or a name.
the type that a System.Type object (typeobject) stands for.

section.para: A name that is no type is an error.

section.title: typeObject
section.para: Returns the System.Type of object, as a NetObject (for a type, the System.Type object of that type): the way to reflection (.net~typeObject(o)~GetMethods).

section.title: typeOf
section.para: Returns the name of the type of the .NET object object (for a type, that type's name), as C# writes it: System.Collections.Generic.List<System.Int32>. A Rexx value is no .NET object: an error.

section.title: unbox
section.para: Returns the Rexx value of a .NET object that holds a number, a bool, a char, a string or an enum value (its name); any other object, and any Rexx value, unchanged.

section.title: NetObject Class
section.para: A .NET object in Rexx: a proxy that holds a handle to the object, by reference. Messages that are not its Rexx methods are the object's .NET members. Its subclasses are NetType (a type, whose messages are its static members), NetArray and NetEnum; a Rexx program can make subclasses of its own ().

row.entry: Methods inherited from the Object class

example.title: NetObject
example.programlisting:
sb = .net~System~Text~StringBuilder~new("abc") say sb~makeString~word(2) sb~Length (sb == sb~Append("d")) sb~Capacity = 100 say sb~ToString sb~Capacity t = .net~System~Threading~Tasks~Task~FromResult(.net~int32(42)) say t~await
::requires "net.cls"

section.title: new (Class Method)
section.para: For a subclass of NetObject, either of two things. If the class (or a superclass) extends a .NET class (), it makes the .NET object with the base's constructor that takes the arguments (). Otherwise, given a netobject, it makes an object of the subclass that stands for the same .NET object: one more proxy, == to it, whose methods come first (). A subclass's own init must call self~init:super(...) with the same arguments. A NetObject is never made from scratch: .NET objects come from &net;.

section.title: Member (unknown)
section.para: Any message that is not a method of the object's Rexx class is a .NET member of the object (): a property or field read, a method call with the arguments, an indexed property read, or an event (a NetEvent). The unknown method that does this is the bridge's; a subclass that defines its own reaches .NET with FORWARD CLASS (SUPER). A name that is no member is SYNTAX 97.1, with a System.MissingMemberException in condition("O")~additional[3] ().

section.title: Member= (unknown)
section.para: Sets the property or field name to value, converted to its type. The member must exist: setting a name the object has not is SYNTAX 97.1, as reading one.

Returns the element at the indexes: the indexer of the object's type (its default member, Item or what the type calls it), from 0 for a list, by key for a dictionary, overloads chosen as for methods (). An array is a NetArray, whose [] counts from 1.
Sets the element at the indexes to value, through the type's indexer.

== and = return &true; if other is a proxy for the same .NET object (object identity, as C#'s ReferenceEquals); the others return the opposite. To compare by .NET's own equality, send a~Equals(b). A NetEnum compares by value ().

section.title: await
section.para: For a Task, a Task<T>, a ValueTask or a ValueTask<T>: waits until it ends, blocking this thread as C#'s .Result does, and returns its result, or nothing for a task without one. A task that failed raises its own exception as SYNTAX 98.900. On a user interface's thread, do not await a task that needs that thread to finish ().

section.title: hashCode
section.para: Returns a hash code that two proxies for the same .NET object share, so that proxies can be indexes of a Rexx Directory, Table or Set. .NET's own is o~GetHashCode.

section.title: makeArray
section.para: Returns a Rexx Array with the items of the object, an IEnumerable, taken now: what DO x OVER o uses ().

section.title: makeString
section.para: Returns a description of the proxy, which SAY and concatenation use: a NetObject (System.Text.StringBuilder #12), the class's name for an instance of a Rexx subclass. .NET's text of the object is o~ToString.

section.title: string
section.para: The .NET member String, if the object or type has one (the type System.String in the namespace System); otherwise makeString.

section.title: supplier
section.para: Returns a Rexx Supplier of the indexes and items of the object, taken now: what DO WITH INDEX i ITEM v OVER o uses. The indexes are those [] takes back: a dictionary's keys, a list's positions from 0, 1 to n for other enumerables ().

section.title: start, send, copy, run, request
section.para: The .NET member of that name, if the object or type has one (process~Start, socket~Send(bytes), .net~System~IO~File~Copy(a, b)); otherwise the method of Rexx's Object class ().

section.title: netExtension (Class Method)
NetType Class
section.para: A .NET type in Rexx, a subclass of NetObject: its messages are its static members, and new makes an instance. A type reached by name is the same object each time. Its System.Type object is .net~typeObject(t).

section.title: new
section.para: Returns a new instance of the type, made by its constructor that takes the arguments (overloads chosen as for methods). A struct without arguments is its default value. The type of a Rexx class that extends a .NET class is made with the class's own new, not this one.

section.title: Static Member (unknown)
section.para: Any other message is a static member of the type: a property or field read (with =, a write), a method call, a nested type, or a static event. .net~System~Math~Max(3, 7), .net~System~Console~Out, .net~System~Environment~SpecialFolder. The members of the System.Type object itself are reached through .

section.title: NetArray Class
section.para: A .NET array in Rexx, a subclass of NetObject that behaves as a Rexx Array: from 1 in every dimension, as BSF4ooRexx's BSF_ARRAY_REFERENCE for Java arrays (). It is not an instance of Rexx's Array class. .NET's own members (Length, Rank, GetValue, 0-based) are reached as for any object.

Returns the element at the positions, from 1 in every dimension. A position out of the array's bounds is .NET's IndexOutOfRangeException (SYNTAX 98.900); 0, a negative or a non-whole position, or the wrong number of them, Rexx's own errors (93.907, 93.924, 93.925, 93.926).

section.title: at
section.para: The same as []; the positions may also come as one Rexx Array (a~at(.array~of(2, 3))).
Sets the element at the positions to item, converted to the array's element type.

section.title: put
section.para: The same as []=, with the item first, as a Rexx Array's put; the positions may also come as one Rexx Array.

section.title: putStrict
section.para: As put, with item converted to type (a name or a NetType) first: for an array of object or of an interface, which would take the item as a string. As BSF4ooRexx's putStrict.

section.title: items
section.para: Returns the number of elements: all of them, as a .NET array has a fixed size (a Rexx Array counts those that hold an item).

section.title: size
section.para: The same as items.

section.title: dimension
section.para: Without an argument, the number of dimensions (the rank); with n, the length of dimension n (0 past the rank, as for a Rexx Array).

section.title: makeArray
section.para: Returns a Rexx Array with every element, row by row (the last position varying fastest), nulls as &nil;: what DO OVER uses.

section.title: supplier
section.para: Returns a Rexx Supplier of the positions (from 1; for a multidimensional array, an Array of positions, as a Rexx Array's supplier gives) and the elements.

section.title: makeString, toString
section.para: As a Rexx Array's: the elements as a string, in storage order, with format "L" (lines, separated by separator, by default .endOfLine) or "C" (characters). SAY and concatenation use makeString, so they show the elements. The type is .net~typeOf(a).

section.title: NetEnum Class
section.para: A .NET enum value in Rexx, a subclass of NetObject, as Java's enum values are objects in BSF4ooRexx. Its string value is its name, so code written for names keeps working; it compares with a name, a number or another value. It goes back to .NET as the enum value, and a name or a number still converts where .NET wants an enum. Its .NET members (HasFlag, CompareTo) are reached as for any object. An enum type gives its values with DO OVER, and its numbers and names with DO WITH.

example.title: NetEnum
example.programlisting:
day = .net~System~DateTime~new(2026, 10, 9)~DayOfWeek say day day~ordinal (day = "friday") (day == "friday") (day = 5) do d over .net~System~DayOfWeek; if d~ordinal < 2 then say d; end do with index n item name over .net~System~DayOfWeek; if n > 4 then say n name; end opt = .net~System~Text~RegularExpressions~RegexOptions both = .net~System~Enum~Parse(.net~typeObject(opt), "IgnoreCase, Multiline") say both (both = "multiline, ignorecase") both~ordinal both~HasFlag(opt~Multiline) r = .net~System~Text~RegularExpressions~Regex~new("^b", "ignorecase, multiline") say r~IsMatch("a" || "0a"x || "B") -- the flags given as a name
::requires "net.cls"
example.screen: Friday 5 1 0 1 Sunday Monday 5 Friday 6 Saturday IgnoreCase, Multiline 1 3 1 1

section.title: name
section.para: Returns the value's name: Friday; for flags, the names .NET gives, IgnoreCase, Multiline; for a value with no name, its number.

section.title: ordinal, value
section.para: Returns the value's number, the enum's underlying value (5 for Friday). .NET enums have no other ordinal than this number.

= returns &true; when the other side is the same value: a name as .NET reads one (caseless; flags in any order and spacing), the value's number, or another NetEnum of the same type and value. Values of two enum types are never equal. The others return the opposite.
== returns &true; when the other side is exactly the value's name, or another NetEnum of the same type and value.

section.title: string, makeString
section.para: The value's name, so that SAY, concatenation and WHEN d = "Friday" read it as one.

section.title: hashCode
section.para: The hash code of the value's name, consistent with ==: a NetEnum is a good index for a Rexx collection.

section.title: NetNamespace Class
section.para: A .NET namespace, which is not a .NET object, only a prefix of type names: each message goes one level down. A namespace reached by name is the same object each time. &net; is the root namespace.

section.title: Namespace or Type (unknown)
section.para: The sub-namespace or the type name (caseless) in this namespace: a NetNamespace or a NetType, remembered once found. A namespace takes no arguments.

section.title: string, makeString
section.para: makeString describes it: a NetNamespace (System.IO). string is the type String of the namespace, if there is one (.net~System~String), else the same as makeString.

section.title: NetRef Class
section.para: A holder for an argument by reference: a ref, out or in parameter of a .NET method (), or a COM argument by reference, as ooRexx's OLEVariant. makeString shows its value: a NetRef (5).

section.title: new (Class Method)
section.para: Returns a new NetRef holding value (default &nil;): the same as .net~ref(value).

section.title: value
section.para: Returns the value it holds: after a call, what the method left in the parameter, as any .NET value comes to Rexx.

section.title: value=
section.para: Sets the value it holds, given to the next call that takes it.

section.title: NetTyped Class
section.para: A Rexx value with a .NET type forced on it, made by .net~int16(x) and its siblings, as, null and named (). It is only a mark for the next call, not a .NET object: box makes one.

row.entry: Methods inherited from the Object class

section.title: kind
section.para: Returns the type it forces, as the bridge records it (System.Int16; null for .net~null).

section.title: value
section.para: Returns the Rexx value it marks.

section.title: NetHandler Class
section.para: A Rexx object and the name of one of its methods, for .NET to call, made by . Given where .NET wants a delegate, it becomes a delegate of that type, the same one each time for the same type, so that -= removes what += added. See .

row.entry: Methods inherited from the Object class

section.title: target
section.para: Returns the Rexx object the handler's message goes to.

section.title: message
section.para: Returns the message's name, uppercased.

section.title: options
section.para: Returns the handler's options, lowercased (queued, latest queued, or empty).

section.title: release
section.para: Ends the handler: its delegates stay valid but do nothing (they return their type's default), its queued calls are dropped, and it can still be given to -=. A handler needs no release: the bridge holds it while .NET can call it (); release stops a handler at once, wherever .NET keeps it.

section.title: released
section.para: Returns &true; once release has been sent.

section.title: NetEvent Class
section.para: An event of a .NET object or type, or of a COM object: o~Click, when the object has an event of that name and no property of it. Its operators add and remove handlers.

row.entry: Methods inherited from the Object class

section.para: Adds (+) or removes (-) handler, a NetHandler or a delegate of the event's type, and returns the event: so o~Click += h, which Rexx runs as o~Click = o~Click + h, adds it (the assignment that follows is a no-op for the same event).

section.title: owner
section.para: Returns the object (or type, for a static event) the event is of.

section.title: name
section.para: Returns the event's name, as .NET writes it.

section.title: NetCall Class
section.para: One call of a queued handler, waiting for a Rexx thread to take it: returns one, and dispatches each it takes. (ooRexx/WASM calls it JSEvent; here NetEvent is the event member.)

example.title: NetHandler, NetEvent and NetCall
example.programlisting:
timer = .net~System~Timers~Timer~new(50) say timer~Elapsed~class~id timer~Elapsed~name h = .net~handler(.Ticker~new, "TICK", "queued") timer~Elapsed += h timer~AutoReset = 0 timer~Start c = .net~nextEvent(5) -- a NetCall, when the timer fires say c~message c~arguments~items .net~typeOf(c~arguments[2]) c~dispatch timer~Elapsed -= h say .net~nextEvent(0.2)
::requires "net.cls" ::class Ticker ::method tick use arg sender, e say "tick from" .net~typeOf(sender)
example.screen: NETEVENT Elapsed TICK 2 System.Timers.ElapsedEventArgs tick from System.Timers.Timer The NIL object

section.title: handler
section.para: Returns the NetHandler that .NET called.

section.title: arguments
section.para: Returns an Array with the delegate's arguments, as .NET values come to Rexx.

section.title: target, message
section.para: The handler's object and message name.

section.title: dispatch
section.para: Sends the handler's message to its object with the call's arguments, on this thread, and returns what the method returns, if anything (a queued delegate has returned already: the result goes nowhere else).
